content: 1. Intranasal administration of midazolam, when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, results in increased systemic exposure to midazolam, potentially prolonging sedation. Avoid or consider alternative drugs. 2. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of midostaurin by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Both clarithromycin and midostaurin prolong the QTc interval, necessitating caution. 3. Mifepristone elevates the levels or effects of clarithromycin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 4. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of mirtazapine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 5. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of modafinil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 6. Clarithromycin and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 7. Nefazodone increases clarithromycin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and clarithromycin increases nefazodone levels similarly. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 8. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of nelfinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 9. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of neratinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid co-administration of neratinib with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 10. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of nevirapine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 11. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of nilotinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 12. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of nirogacestat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 13. Both nortriptyline and clarithromycin prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 14. Both clarithromycin and octreotide prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 15. Clarithromycin and olanzapine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Limited data suggest olanzapine may rarely cause significant QTc prolongation. 16. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of olaparib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the olaparib dose to 150 mg (capsule) or 100 mg (tablet) twice daily. Do not substitute tablets with capsules. 17. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of omaveloxolone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the omaveloxolone dose to 50 mg/day and monitor closely for adverse effects. 18. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 19. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir and dasabuvir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 20. Clarithromycin and ondansetron both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid in patients with congenital long QT syndrome; ECG monitoring is recommended with concomitant medications that prolong QT interval, electrolyte abnormalities, CHF, or bradyarrhythmias. 21. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of ondansetron by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 22. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of osimertinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid co-administration of osimertinib with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If no alternative exists, monitor the patient closely for adverse effects. 23. Clarithromycin and oxaliplatin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 24. Clarithromycin increases oxycodone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Oxycodone dose reduction may be warranted when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 25. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of palbociclib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid co-administration of palbociclib with strong CYP3A inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the palbociclib dose to 75 mg/day. 26. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of palovarotene by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 27. Clarithromycin and panobinostat both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Panobinostat significantly prolongs the QT interval, and its prescribing information advises against use with drugs known to prolong QTc. 28. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of pazopanib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is necessary, reduce the pazopanib dose to 400 mg/day. 29. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of pemigatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pemigatinib dose as per the drug monograph. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for three elimination half-lives. 30. Both perphenazine and clarithromycin prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 31. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of pexidartinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pexidartinib dose as per the drug monograph. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for three elimination half-lives. 32. Clarithromycin increases the effects of phenindione by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 33. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of pimavanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 34. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of pirtobrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the pirtobrutinib dose by 50 mg. If the current dose is 50 mg daily, discontinue pirtobrutinib during the use of strong CYP3A inhibitors. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the inhibitor for five half-lives. 35. Clarithromycin and pitolisant both prolong the QTc interval. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of pitolisant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 36. Clarithromycin increases pomalidomide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 37. Clarithromycin increases the levels of ponatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the ponatinib starting dose to 30 mg daily. 38. Clarithromycin and ponesimod both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 39. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of pralsetinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 40. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of prednisone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 41. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of primaquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 42. Clarithromycin and procainamide both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 43. Both prochlorperazine and clarithromycin prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 44. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of progesterone intravaginal gel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 45. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of micronized progesterone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 46. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of natural progesterone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 47. Both promazine and clarithromycin prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 48. Both promethazine and clarithromycin prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 49. Clarithromycin and propafenone both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 50. Clarithromycin increases the effects of protamine by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 51. Both protriptyline and clarithromycin prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 52. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of quetiapine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 53. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of quinidine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 54. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases clarithromycin levels by decreasing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of prolonged QTc interval. 55. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of ranolazine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 56. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of repaglinide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 57. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of repotrectinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 58. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of resmetirom by other mechanisms (refer to comments). Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid co-administration of resmetirom (an OATP1B1/3 substrate) with OATP1B1/3 inhibitors. 59. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of ribociclib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 60. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of rifabutin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 61. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of rimegepant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 62. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of ritonavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 63. Clarithromycin increases rivaroxaban levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid concomitant use of rivaroxaban with combined P-gp and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. However, in patients with normal renal function, no precautions are necessary as the change in exposure is unlikely to affect bleeding risk. Avoid in patients with mild to moderately impaired renal function (CrCl 15-80 mL/min). 64. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of romidepsin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors should be avoided if possible. 65. Clarithromycin increases the toxicity of rosuvastatin by other mechanisms (refer to comments). Avoid or use an alternative drug. OATP1B1 inhibitors may increase the risk of myopathy. 66. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of ruxolitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Reduce the ruxolitinib starting dose to 10 mg BID with platelet counts ≥100 x 10^9/L and concurrent use of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Avoid with platelet counts <100 x 10^9/L. 67. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of ruxolitinib topical by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Reduce the ruxolitinib starting dose to 10 mg BID with platelet counts ≥100 x 10^9/L and concurrent use of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Avoid with platelet counts <100 x 10^9/L. 68. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of selpercatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 69. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of selumetinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the selumetinib dosage (refer to the selumetinib monograph for further information). Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the inhibitor for three elimination half-lives. 70. Both sertraline and clarithromycin prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 71. Both sevoflurane and clarithromycin prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 72. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of sildenafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug.
